newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan king to inaugurate $968 mln dam.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan king to inaugurate $968 mln dam.

text.p: Moroccan King Hassan and Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro will inaugurate a nine billion dirham ($968 million) dam and power plant on Thursday, bringing to one million hectares (2.5 million acres) Morocco's irrigated farming area.

"This is the biggest dam Morocco has ever had, we will not be able to build another one of that importance in the future because of its exceptional site," Public Works Minister Abdelaziz Meziane told a news conference on Tuesday.
The Italian president was due to arrive later on Tuesday for a three-day visit to Morocco.
Al Wahda dam, 125 kms (78 miles) east of Rabat, will have a capacity of 3.8 billion cubic metres, equal to 40 percent of the capacity of the country's 90 other dams.

Meziane said it would irrigate 100,000 hectares (250,000 acres), generate an annual 400 million kilowatts of hydroelectric energy and later provide 600 million cubic metres of drinking water to the Casablanca region.
It will also allow for the building of four small and medium-sized dams upstream.
The public works ministry said it expected some 40,000 to 50,000 jobs to be created.

The project, for which construction started in June 1991, has been financed by Italy at 34 percent, Morocco 22.3 percent, Spain 20 percent, the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development and the Kuwaiti Fund a total of 22 percent, and Russia 1.7 percent.
